class.name: TTSPersona
class.brief_description: A text to speech voice with its settings, used by [TTSServer].

members.member: If [code]true[/code], speaking with this persona stops the current utterance and clears the queue first. If [code]false[/code], the text is added to the end of the queue.

The language of the persona, such as [code]"en"[/code] or [code]"en_US"[/code]. Used to find a voice when [member voice] is empty or does not exist on this machine. [code]"en"[/code] matches every English voice, [code]"en_US"[/code] prefers American English. Hyphens and underscores are treated the same. If empty, the language of the system ([method OS.get_locale]) is used.

The name of the persona. [TTSServer] uses it as the key in its persona list ([method TTSServer.add_persona], [method TTSServer.get_persona]). It is separate from [member Resource.resource_name]. [b]Note:[/b] The persona list keeps the name the persona had when it was added. After renaming a persona, add it again.
The voice pitch, from [code]0.0[/code] (lowest) to [code]2.0[/code] (highest). [code]1.0[/code] is the default pitch of the voice. Values outside this range are clamped.

The speech rate, from [code]0.1[/code] (slowest) to [code]10.0[/code] (fastest). [code]1.0[/code] is the normal rate of the voice. Values outside this range are clamped. Some platforms limit the range further (for example, Linux maps it to about [code]0.5[/code] to [code]2.5[/code]).

The voice to speak with: an [code]"id"[/code] or a [code]"name"[/code] from [method TTSServer.get_voices]. Names are usually more stable across machines than IDs. If empty or not found, a voice for [member language] is used.
The volume, from [code]0[/code] (silent) to [code]100[/code] (loudest). Values outside this range are clamped.
